{{Short description|Generalization in mathematics}}
In [[category theory]], a branch of [[mathematics]], '''profunctors''' are a generalization of [[binary relation|relations]] and also of [[bimodule]]s.

== Definition ==

A '''profunctor''' (also named '''[[:fr:Distributeur (théorie des catégories)|distributor]]''' by the French school and '''module''' by the Sydney school) <math>\,\phi</math> from a [[category (mathematics)|category]] <math>C</math> to a category <math>D</math>, written
: <math>\phi : C\nrightarrow D</math>,
is defined to be a [[functor (category theory)|functor]]
: <math>\phi : D^{\mathrm{op}}\times C\to\mathbf{Set}</math>
where <math>D^\mathrm{op}</math> denotes the [[opposite category]] of <math>D</math> and <math>\mathbf{Set}</math> denotes the [[category of sets]]. Given morphisms <math> f : d\to d', g : c\to c'</math> respectively in <math> D, C </math> and an element <math> x\in\phi(d',c)</math>, we write <math>xf\in \phi(d,c), gx\in\phi(d',c')</math> to denote the actions.

Using that the [[category of small categories]] <math>\mathbf{Cat}</math> is [[cartesian closed category|cartesian closed]], the profunctor <math>\phi</math> can be seen as a functor
: <math>\hat{\phi} : C\to\hat{D}</math>
where <math>\hat{D}</math> denotes the category <math>\mathrm{Set}^{D^\mathrm{op}}</math> of [[presheaf (category theory)|presheaves]] over <math>D</math>.

A '''correspondence''' from <math> C </math> to <math> D</math> is a profunctor <math> D\nrightarrow C</math>.

=== Profunctors as categories ===

An equivalent definition of a profunctor <math>\phi : C\nrightarrow D</math> is a category whose objects are the [[disjoint union]] of the objects of <math>C</math> and the objects of <math>D</math>, and whose morphisms are the morphisms of <math>C</math> and the morphisms of <math>D</math>, plus zero or more additional morphisms from objects of <math>D</math> to objects of <math>C</math>. The sets in the formal definition above are the hom-sets between objects of <math>D</math> and objects of <math>C</math>. (These are also known as het-sets, since the corresponding morphisms can be called ''heteromorphisms''.) The previous definition can be recovered by the restriction of the hom-functor <math>\phi^\text{op}\times \phi \to \mathbf{Set}</math> to <math>D^\text{op}\times C</math>.

This also makes it clear that a profunctor can be thought of as a relation between the objects of <math>C</math> and the objects of <math>D</math>, where each member of the relation is associated with a set of morphisms. A functor is a special case of a profunctor in the same way that a function is a special case of a relation.

=== Composition of profunctors ===

The composite <math>\psi\phi</math> of two profunctors
: <math>\phi : C\nrightarrow D</math> and <math>\psi : D\nrightarrow E</math>
is given by
: <math>\psi\phi=\mathrm{Lan}_{Y_D}(\hat{\psi})\circ\hat\phi</math>
where <math>\mathrm{Lan}_{Y_D}(\hat{\psi})</math> is the left [[Kan extension]] of the functor <math>\hat{\psi}</math> along the [[Yoneda functor]] <math>Y_D : D\to\hat D</math> of <math>D</math> (which to every object <math>d</math> of <math>D</math> associates the functor <math>D(-,d) : D^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Set}</math>).

It can be shown that
: <math>(\psi\phi)(e,c)=\left(\coprod_{d\in D}\psi(e,d)\times\phi(d,c)\right)\Bigg/\sim</math>
where <math>\sim</math> is the least [[equivalence relation]] such that <math>(y',x')\sim(y,x)</math> whenever there exists a morphism <math>v</math> in <math>D</math> such that
: <math>y'=vy \in\psi(e,d')</math>  and  <math>x'v=x \in\phi(d,c)</math>.
Equivalently, profunctor composition can be written using a [[End_(category_theory)|coend]]
: <math>(\psi\phi)(e,c)=\int^{d\colon D}\psi(e,d)\times\phi(d,c)</math>

=== Bicategory of profunctors ===

Composition of profunctors is associative only up to isomorphism (because the product is not strictly associative in '''Set'''). The best one can hope is therefore to build a [[bicategory]] '''Prof''' whose
* 0-cells are [[small category|small categories]],
* 1-cells between two small categories are the profunctors between those categories,
* 2-cells between two profunctors are the [[natural transformation]]s between those profunctors.

== Properties ==
=== Lifting functors to profunctors ===
A functor <math>F : C\to D</math> can be seen as a profunctor <math>\phi_F : C\nrightarrow D</math> by postcomposing with the Yoneda functor:
: <math>\phi_F=Y_D\circ F</math>.

It can be shown that such a profunctor <math>\phi_F</math> has a [[Adjoint functors|right adjoint]]. Moreover, this is a characterization: a profunctor <math>\phi : C\nrightarrow D</math> has a right adjoint if and only if <math>\hat\phi : C\to\hat D</math> factors through the [[Karoubi envelope|Cauchy completion]] of <math>D</math>, i.e. there exists a functor <math>F : C\to D</math> such that <math>\hat\phi=Y_D\circ F</math>.
